title: ignite-week-90-day-onramp-and-exec-slate-v0-1
content:
Purpose

This is a working brief for Ignite Week (company kickoff for the upcoming 90-day sprint). The doc combines an early OKR proposal, executive update talking points, and a lightweight all-staff agenda + comms kit intended for rapid iteration. Treat as the single source for the next two weeks of alignment prep; content is intentionally terse and written for rapid edits.

TL;DR (for execs)
- Goal: Re-center the company on measurable delivery across reliability, cost-per-token, and developer adoption.
- Proposed top-line OKRs: Improve serving reliability to 99.9% SLO, reduce hosted token cost by 18% for high-throughput customers, and increase integration (SDK + quickstarts) activation by 40% in target cohorts.
- Ask: Execs to confirm runway (resourcing) for Dedicated capacity pilot, approve one-week canary window for new batching service, and join the Ignite townline (20min) to endorse priorities.

Context / constraints
- Recent incidents (Dec) exposed edge-case degradation during autoscale. SRE and Runtime teams have a mitigation plan but need cross-team alignment for testing windows.
- Sales pipeline shows two enterprise pilots asking for Private deployment onboarding in Q2; this shifts some priority to on-prem packaging and supportability docs.
- Budget sensitivity: product ops needs to balance cost optimizations (quantization pilot) vs. UX regressions. We must pair each suggested quant profile with a quality evaluation plan.

Draft OKRs (90-day window) — very early
O1: Serving reliability (customer-facing)
- KR1: Achieve 99.9% availability on hosted endpoints for p95 latency under baseline traffic
- KR2: Reduce production incident MTTR from 45m -> 15m for scale-related cases
- KR3: Run two cross-team game days and close top-5 repeat failure modes

O2: Unit economics & cost tooling
- KR1: Reduce average token cost for high-throughput customers by 18% through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations
- KR2: Ship automated batch-suggester to Redwood Console and onboard 3 pilot customers
- KR3: Publish a public benchmark comparing cost/latency across canonical workloads (small doc + reproducible harness)

O3: Developer activation and retention (PLG motion)
- KR1: Increase SDK adoption (instrumented calls) by 40% in target cohort (startups, platform teams)
- KR2: Launch 3 new quickstarts (chatbot, semantically-search, reranking) and measure time-to-first-success < 30m
- KR3: Decrease docs friction score from baseline by 25% (survey + support tickets)

Notes on OKRs: these are intentionally fewer and cross-functional. If execs want more product-feature KRs, we can spawn sub-KRs for Dedicated and Private in the next pass.

Exec update talking points (3 minutes each)
- Quick orientation: where we are (stable growth in hosted API usage, uptick in enterprise interest), top risks (autoscale edge-case, quantization QoE), and near-term asks (resource sanction for Dedicated pilot, executive sloting for Ignite townline).
- Highlight wins: runtime kernel improvements delivered in Dec lowered p99 on short sequences by ~12% (link PR), Optimize toolkit alpha trials showing 10–12% cost wins for select customers.
- Ask for alignment: one-week canary for new batch-suggester (target window: Feb 8–14), Exec sponsor for Private pilot (customer X onboarding), and explicit sign-off on QA acceptance criteria for quantized models.

All-staff Ignite Agenda (1-hour compact format)
- 00:00 – 00:05: Welcome + framing (CEO)
- 00:05 – 00:12: State of the product + commercial snapshot (Head of Product + CRO)
- 00:12 – 00:22: Reliability & cost focus (Eng lead) — measurable asks and short-term mitigations
- 00:22 – 00:32: Developer adoption playbook (DX lead) — quickstarts and SDK roadmap
- 00:32 – 00:42: Customer spotlight (Solutions eng) — pilot learnings and ask for volunteers
- 00:42 – 00:52: Breakout charge + micro-commitments (team leads)
- 00:52 – 01:00: Exec close + top-level asks (Founders)

Notes: Make the townline active — micro-commitments at the end are required from each team (one measurable deliverable in 30 days). Keep slides to < 12. We will record and surface a 1-page action tracker.

Comms plan (rollout + owners)
- Internal doc (this file) = canonical. Product Ops (Nora) owner.
- Pre-Ignite: Ops brief to execs (EOD Jan 25) — owners: Nora + Ethan.
- Day-of: single-slide email + short TL;DR in Slack #all (Maya to prepare).
- Post-event (within 48h): action tracker published, OKR update sent to managers, and short video snippet of exec close (Marketing to coordinate).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Decision: approve Dedicated pilot resourcing (2 FTEs + 50% infra spend) — We need sign-off from CFO/Head of Sales.
- Decision: acceptance threshold for quantized profiles — Should we accept up to 3% BLEU/ROUGE/embedded-sim loss? Need standards from Applied ML.
- Question: Can SRE support a one-week canary if we run it in parallel across two regions? If not, propose a staged rollout with canary in region A then B.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization -> Mitigation: pair each quant rollout with A/B regression evals and rollback hooks in runtime.
- Risk: Customer churn during canary window if latency blips -> Mitigation: select low-risk pilot customers and provide dedicated support channel.

Quick TODOs (who to ping now)
- Ethan: draft exec one-pager (2 sides) and include recommended resource ask — due Jan 20
- Maya: prepare the townline slide deck skeleton + Slack TL;DR — due Jan 23
- Liam: coordinate with SRE on canary window feasibility and game day schedule — due Jan 21
- Applied ML: create baseline quality thresholds for quant profiles and share by Jan 24

Notes to self (working, rough)
- Keep language tight for exec OnePager. Avoid product feature laundry lists — focus on measurable impact and ask.
- Consider a short customer-facing explainer on Dedicated benefits for pilots (private vs dedicated clarity).
- Add a feedback loop: 2-week cadence for short OKR check-ins during the 90-day window.

Appendix (links & artifacts)

- Cost harness (internal bench): gs://rwd-infer/cost-bench/q1-alpha
- Draft quickstarts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/tree/ignite
